args.value: Faros-case: a deterministic, human-supervised knowledge tree mapping Faros AI's offering to a buyer persona (Maya), with Claude-managed advisor + curator agents that answer 'how can Faros help?' from approved nodes only. Repo: aliomraniH/Faros-case. Surfaces: Claude web (seed), Cowork/Desktop (fetch+commit). Goal endstate: run an advisor-vs-persona Q&A simulation.

Three rules make it deterministic, not vibes: (1) agents TRAVERSE approved nodes, humans AUTHOR/approve; (2) every node is typed + carries provenance (sourced|inferred|user-intent) and an honesty label (shipped|roadmap|inference); (3) the tree is the contract — advisor answers cite node IDs or say 'not in the approved tree'. One human gate: approval. Mirrors Faros's own policy+provenance+human-review governance.

Knowledge node schema at schemas/knowledge-node.schema.json. Types: organization|faros|persona|flow|principle|mapping. Required: id,type,title,parent,provenance,status. Agents write status=proposed; only a human sets approved (requires approved_by). sourced provenance requires a source block (url+retrieved_at). 13 seed nodes all validate (0 errors).

Two agents, roles never blur: CURATOR reads fetch/raw/*.json and proposes nodes (status=proposed, never approves own work); ADVISOR answers persona questions from APPROVED nodes only, returns a structured contract with citations + honesty label + positioning_check (door/room, empower-not-police), and emits a curator task on gaps instead of improvising.

Faros thesis (validated against Jun 2026 site): trace every AI token to the work it produced and the outcome it shipped. 'Your AI vendors tell you what you spent; Faros tells you what it produced.' Token Intelligence built on a Token Attribution Ledger + Engineering World Model. Sequence: understand spend -> optimize workflows -> maximize outcomes ('outcome maxxing > token maxxing'). Door=spend, room=outcomes/quality; explicitly NOT FinOps cost-cutting.

Three pillars: OBSERVE (shipped) — operational graph joining ticket->session->PR->deploy->incident->spend at session/file/decision grain; OPTIMIZE (partial) — model/workflow recommendations, repo skills/rules, historical replay; GOVERN (partial) — central policy, distributed context, provenance/audit, compensating controls (feature-flag) over hard blocks, human still reviews+merges.

Proof points: Vimeo ~+30% Copilot adoption (vendor case study); SmartBear hours/days reporting -> minutes (vendor case study); MIT NANDA: 95% of enterprise AI no measurable P&L impact, a learning gap not model quality (INDEPENDENT — the credibility anchor). Connectors: 70+ (press-release era) now marketed as 100+. Company: founded 2019, San Mateo, ~$36M (SignalFire/Lobby Capital), ex-Salesforce Einstein team (Vitaly Gordon CEO, Shubha Nabar, Matthew Tovbin).

Two facts to keep accurate in the room: (1) EU AI Act — Aug 2 2026 was the ORIGINAL high-risk deadline; the Digital Omnibus defers it to Dec 2 2027, though transparency rules + the original date remain live pending formal adoption. Don't state Aug 2026 full-obligations as settled. (2) The '~18-month competitive window' is an INFERENCE, not a cited stat — present as interpretive framing. Causal attribution = double/debiased ML via EconML (CATE, R-score gating); concede limits honestly.

Primary buyer persona: Maya, VP Platform Engineering, ~1,200-eng B2B SaaS, ~90% AI adoption, renewal coming, board ROI pressure. The squeeze: board above ('justify the spend'), developers below ('help not surveil'); Maya in the middle answers up without policing down. Owns the problem; CFO opens the door; staff engineer guards the gate; developers decide if it lives.

OPEN: how Faros itself is priced is the cleanest FinOps-vs-platform tell. Ali's intended call: platform/outcome pricing (seats / connected-org tier), NOT consumption or savings-based, because consumption pricing structurally bends the product toward 'spend less' and collapses the positioning. Public anchor seen: ~$29/contributor/month, ~4:1 ROI. Confirm on live fetch.

Live faros.ai offering as fetched 2026-06-26 (Cowork batch-1). PLATFORM is one product framed as six foundational capabilities: Enterprise-Grade, Analytics, AI for Productivity, Interoperability, Customization, Catalogs. CAPABILITIES nav names five product surfaces: (1) Token Intelligence — trace/classify AI token spend productive|inefficient|wasteful, attribute to team/task, keep/scope/cut tool verdicts; built on Engineering World Model + Token Attribution Ledger (both presented shipped); (2) AI Transformation — causal-analysis ROI, cohort/A-B tests, CFO-ready reports, GAINS maturity framework, IDE governance/guardrails; (3) Context for AI Agents (branded 'Clara') — bootstrap agents with tribal knowledge from past PRs, agentic PR delivery with Claude/Codex/Copilot/Cursor, human-in-the-loop, continuous learning; (4) Developer Productivity — DORA/SPACE/DevEx dashboards, surveys, benchmarks, AI Assistant in Slack/Teams/IDE; (5) Predictable Roadmap Delivery — initiative tracking, delay/overrun forecasting, capacity analytics, software cost capitalization (a planning/PMO surface OUTSIDE the seed's Observe/Optimize/Govern thesis — taxonomy flag). SOLUTIONS have no /solutions index page; reached via role pages (ai-leaders, engineering-executives, platform-engineering-devex-leaders, program-managers) and use-case pages. Positioning confirmed by homepage hero 'stop tokenmaxxing, start outcome maxxing' and 'smarter—not smaller—budgets' (matches repo's money-is-the-door discipline). Company: founded by ex-Salesforce Einstein team (Vitaly Gordon CEO, Shubha Nabar Chief Scientist, Matthew Tovbin CTO); vision 'engineering at the speed of ideas'; certs SOC2/ISO27001/GDPR/CSA STAR; 100+ integrations; stats 10x PR velocity / 40% fewer failed outcomes / 1-day POC; stated price floor $29 per contributor per module per month. Conflicts flagged for human: Optimize (historical-replay, model-routing) and Govern (guardrails) read more shipped on live pages than seed marks them (partial/roadmap).
